entities.summary:
Theodore of Raithu (theodore-of-raithu) was a Christian theologian considered the last of the Neo-Chalcedonians.

As a key figure in the Christian theology of the 7th century, Theodore of Raithu played a crucial role in shaping the theological landscape of the Eastern Roman Empire. Born in the region of Raithu (modern-day Turkey), Theodore rose to prominence as a prominent theologian and scholar, influencing the development of the Eastern Orthodox Church. His work focused on the Christological debates of the time, and he was known for his defense of the Neo-Chalcedonian formula.

Theodore's significance can be seen in the Council of Constantinople (630 CE), where he participated as a delegate, and the subsequent development of the Eastern Orthodox Church. His work also had an impact on the theological debates of the time, influencing the writing of John of Damascus.

Theodore's legacy can be seen in the continued development of the Eastern Orthodox Church, which he helped shape through his theological contributions. His work also had a lasting impact on the theology of the Eastern Roman Empire, influencing the development of the Church's doctrine on the nature of Christ.

Theodore of Raithu was a scholar who contributed to the theological debates of the 7th century, shaping the theological landscape of the Eastern Roman Empire.
